authors: Bou, X., Vincent, E., Facciolo, G., Grompone von Gioi, R., Morel, J.-M. & Ehret, T.
title: Remote sensing change detection via weak temporal supervision
relevance: Fits our asset list better than STAR (ID 191) because it exploits the thing STAR ignores - additional TEMPORAL OBSERVATIONS of a single-temporal labelled dataset, with no new annotations. Its two assumptions map onto us directly: pairs from the SAME location across dates predominantly contain no real change, while pairs from DIFFERENT locations synthesise change examples. We hold exactly this: one labelled year plus seventeen unlabelled acquisitions of the same city. The elegant part for us is that same-location cross-era pairs teach the model 'these look different but nothing changed', which is precisely the sensor/era INVARIANCE that thirty iterations identified as our core problem - so one mechanism addresses both the label shortage and the domain shift that Search 53 said would have to be composed separately. PREPRINT, and the no-change assumption weakens as the temporal gap grows, so short-gap pairs are the safe training material.
